xwhatsapp-strokecopylinkgoogleAdd Al Jazeera on GoogleinfoRescue workers and residents during a search operation after a roof collapsed at a school in Peshawar, Pakistan [AFP]By Al Jazeera Staff, AP and ReutersPublished On 15 Oct 202615 Oct 2026The roof of a school in northwestern Pakistan has collapsed, killing at least 32 students and a teacher and injuring more than 45 others, authorities and rescue officials said.

The incident happened on Thursday at Al-Khair Education Centre, a private school in Peshawar, the capital of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province.

Mohammad Asim, spokesman for Lady Reading Hospital, where many victims were transported, said the fatalities include 12 girls and a female teacher. He added that some of the injured were in critical condition.

Most of the children killed or injured were between six and 12 years old, and the oldest was 14, Asim said. The hospital has declared an emergency as medical staff treat the wounded.

At least 45 children suffered injuries, ranging from minor wounds to severe trauma, said Arif Khattak, regional director of the Rescue Department.

Television footage showed rescuers clawing through debris with their bare hands and carrying bloodied children to waiting ambulances as residents crowded the narrow alley where the school stood.

A ‌higher-floor roof collapsed onto classrooms below, crumpling two storeys of the building, a rescue official said.

Hours after the collapse, rescue officials said everyone trapped under the rubble had been recovered. An emergency services spokesperson, Bilal Faizi, said that nearly 100 rescuers helped the operation, including parents who helped the crew.

He credited the rapid evacuation with saving at least 40 lives. More than a dozen children suffered minor injuries, he said.

Peshawar’s police chief Saeed Ahmed said that the owner of the school has been arrested. He said the building was structurally weak.

However, following his arrest, the owner, Mohammad Khan, blamed this week’s rains for weakening one of the roofs, according to police, who said the investigation was still under way.

The provincial government said a committee had been formed to investigate the cause of the roof collapse of the three-storey building.

In Islamabad, President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif expressed sorrow over the deaths and offered condolences to the bereaved families in separate statements.

“The entire nation shares the grief of the affected families in this hour of sorrow,” Zardari said.
